source.title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations in Superposition
source.authors: Sunny Liu; Habon A. Issa; André Longon; Liv Gorton; Meenakshi Khosla; Alex H. Williams; David A. Klindt

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper’s analyses and experiments refine how alignment should be interpreted: raw-activation alignment can be deflated by different encoding geometries even when feature content is shared. It also examines alignment across projection dimensions and compares several linear metrics.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from Gaussian-projection simulations, trained sparse autoencoders, and pretrained vision encoders. It also discusses a reported model-size/alignment trend and cites work on local alignment, but those cited results are not this study’s results. No vision-language paired image-caption experiment or model capability sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The study's own pretrained-model result (DINO/CLIP layer pairs on ImageNet val) shows measured cross-model alignment depends on the representation space measured: raw activations versus SAE latents. That bears on V6. The rest is analytic theory and toy simulations (random Gaussian projections, SAEs trained on stipulated latents). These argue that raw-activation linear alignment understates shared features under superposition. They involve no independently trained models of the kind the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that linear alignment on raw activations mixes feature content with encoding geometry (the Gram matrices) and can understate shared features under superposition. SAE-recovered latents restore alignment in simulation, fully with supervision and mostly without. In pretrained vision encoders, SAE-latent alignment exceeds raw alignment, which they read as consistent with superposition. They also suggest the model-size alignment trend may reflect larger models compressing features less.
record.recipe_differences: Uses analytic derivations, Gaussian-projection simulations, TopK sparse autoencoders, and linear alignment metrics; it does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis scale-and-performance analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment changes with projection dimension/compression and with measuring raw activations versus recovered SAE latents. The paper reports that RSA, linear CKA, and linear-regression R2 track closely in the full-overlap simulations.

fits_no_version.finding: With identical feature content, raw-activation RSA, linear CKA and regression R2 all rise monotonically with projection dimension, roughly as m/(m+n-2). The three metrics track each other. The authors offer this as an explanation of the reported model-size alignment trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under linear superposition, raw-activation alignment between systems sharing features scales with neuron count relative to feature count, independent of feature content.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairs with partial feature overlap but less compression can score higher linear CKA than fully overlapping, more compressed pairs (rank inversion).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw-activation alignment orderings need not reflect feature-overlap orderings when compression differs.

fits_no_version.finding: Different-seed SAEs encoding identical latents have deflated raw alignment. Recovered latents restore alignment near 1.0 in the compressed-sensing regime, and unsupervised SAE latents recover most of it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy superposition systems, alignment measured in recovered latent space exceeds raw-activation alignment and approaches the shared-feature ceiling.

record.problems: The pretrained-model study is restricted to vision encoders and reports aggregate figure trends rather than individual numeric comparisons. The paper does not measure capability or conduct a real-model size sweep. Its theoretical analysis assumes white i.i.d. latents, and its synthetic supervised experiments stipulate shared ground-truth features.

untested.parts: No sweep over real model size or capability. The only 'scale' sweep is projection dimension in random Gaussian projections. The model-size trend is only discussed via cited work.
Shared features are imposed by supervised training on stipulated latents. Whether ordinarily trained networks from different seeds learn shared features is not tested on real networks.
No readable per-pair map quality between pretrained models. No stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No recurrence of interpretable features, neurons or circuits across models is measured.
Local or kNN metrics and their settings, alternative stimulus datasets, and out-of-distribution inputs are not tested. RSA and CKA are compared only in toy simulations.
No plateau test. No test of shared data or objectives versus a common-world account. Raw alignment levels in the pretrained pairs are figure only.

missing.what: The abstract claims results on pretrained language model SAEs. The body reports only DINO/CLIP, and the Limitations say evaluation is restricted to vision encoders. No language-model results exist to record.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 supports/limits labels and its V6 challenge rested on toy random projections. These are not independently trained models, so they were removed. V3, V4 and V7 links were also removed: shared features are stipulated by construction, and the toy maps are not between real models. The only real-model row is R13, and its numbers are figure only. Joint SAE training with a cross-decoding loss could inflate latent alignment, so the V6 support should be read with that caveat.

versions.untested_parts: The dimension sweep is over synthetic projection systems, not a sweep of actual model sizes, capabilities, architectures, objectives, or training data.
No paired image-caption vision-language models or cross-modal performance sweep.

The supervised experiments stipulate shared ground-truth latents; they do not test whether ordinary task-trained networks independently discover the same features. The unsupervised SAE results are on constructed systems, not a sweep of naturally trained networks or their individual units.
Tests linear-regression alignment and SAE-latent-to-activation alignment. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired inputs.
No recurrence of interpretable features, neurons, or circuits is measured.

Compares RSA, linear CKA, and linear regression and compares raw activations with SAE latents. Does not vary the stimulus dataset or test out-of-distribution inputs, neighbour counts, or other local-similarity settings.

Tests incomplete raw alignment and encoding geometry as a cause of apparent misalignment. Does not compare shared training data or objectives against a common-world explanation, or establish a plateau in model alignment.

rows.measure: Pearson r between OLS predictions and targets
rows.value: Figure only; text says latent alignment exceeds raw alignment for the majority of tested system pairs and layers
rows.note: SAEs are trained jointly so the two systems share a sparse latent space. The paper reports the aggregate as a majority, not individual model-pair values.
rows.check: Latent alignment exceeds raw alignment for the majority of the 1260 points, so measured cross-model alignment depends on the representation space. Values are figure only. The SAEs are trained jointly with a cross-decoding loss into a shared latent space, which may build some alignment in by construction. Latent-to-activation and activation-to-activation scores are not strictly like-for-like. The raw scatter (about 0.2–1.0) can't be read per pair, so V4 cannot be determined.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic Gaussian projections across the tested m and k sweeps
reader_labels.reason: Alignment rises monotonically with projection dimension for all three reported metrics, as described in R1–R3.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The sweep varies projection dimension and compression, not actual model size or capability; R1–R3 do not establish the full claim about larger and more capable independently trained models.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Independently trained supervised TopK SAEs on stipulated shared sparse latents in the CS regime
reader_labels.reason: Recovered-latent alignment is reported near 1.0 even while raw activation alignment is deflated, in R5–R8.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Unsupervised latent alignment is above raw alignment but remains between the raw baseline and supervised ceiling; the shared latent content is not shown to emerge in ordinary task-trained networks, in R9–R12.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Recovered latents mapped to other-system activations in the supervised synthetic CS regime
reader_labels.reason: Linear-regression alignment is reported near 1.0 after latent recovery in R7–R8.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: SAE-latent-to-activation alignment is higher than raw alignment for a majority, not all, of the reported pairs; the figure does not provide individual numeric values, in R13–R14.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: RSA, linear CKA, and linear regression on full-overlap Gaussian projections
reader_labels.reason: The three metrics track one another tightly and share the reported monotonic dimension trend, rather than showing the trend vanishing under these alternative linear measures, in R1–R3.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Raw activations versus recovered SAE latents
reader_labels.reason: Alignment differs substantially between raw and latent representations, while the study does not test alternate stimulus datasets or out-of-distribution inputs, in R5–R14.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic systems with shared stipulated latent content
reader_labels.reason: Raw alignment is reduced by compression despite shared features, and partial-overlap pairs can outrank fully overlapping but more compressed pairs, in R1–R8.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pretrained vision model-layer pairs and constructed SAE systems
reader_labels.reason: The reported pretrained comparison is only an aggregate majority, and the study attributes apparent misalignment to encoding geometry without testing shared training data/objectives against a common-world account, in R9–R14.
